notes.t: From Central Alta: west from the beacon checker, past the gun tower, along the power lines; where the Cardiff Pass track meets the south-facing Flagstaff Shoulder, switchback up the shoulder. The last few hundred feet are steeper. 1,630 ft and 0.8 mi to False Flagstaff, 1,960 ft and 1.1 mi to the real summit.
The peak you see from the road is False Flagstaff; the real summit is 0.25 mi northwest and 300 ft higher. Car-to-car is under two hours.
Avoid getting pulled into the gullies on the south face: they narrow your options and add avalanche risk.

notes.t: Start at the "Are you beeping?" sign, head west a few hundred feet, then northwest toward Cardiff Pass along the power poles. Past the Flagstaff turn-off, a track splits off the Cardiff Pass trail and climbs Toledo Bowl.
Of the three, Toledo Bowl is the mellowest, Toledo Face is wide and even, and Toledo Chute is steeper but less chute-like than its name.
Powder Project: the chute drops straight off the top, steepest at the entrance, then eases into an apron and easy skiing to the road. 641 ft, max 37°.
The trailhead is sometimes closed during avalanche mitigation; respect it.

warn.t: UAC's Alta to Cardiff Pass and Alta to Superior route pages both name the Toledo avalanche path; the Cardiff Pass track spends about a mile and 1,500 ft under significant avalanche terrain.

published.what: Two Dogs from Central Alta (to the ridge)

notes.t: Follow the Flagstaff track to False Flagstaff, walk about 500 ft west along the ridge and drop north into Days Fork. Most people mean the run that starts by a prominent rock on the ridge; some mean the whole NE slope between False Flagstaff and Flagstaff.
Two Dogs is named for two dogs killed here on March 8, 1981, when a skier left the traverse and triggered a slide.

This drops into Days Fork, on the Big Cottonwood side. Upper Days Fork is about 1,500 ft from Alta to the ridge versus 2,800 ft from the Spruces lot in Big Cottonwood, so most people climb back to the ridge; the other exit is lower Days Fork to the Spruces trailhead (3.2 mi) with a car or bus shuttle.
The Reddit post calls this an easier LCC tour. WBSkiing rates Two Dogs advanced.

warn.t: UAC's Alta to Flagstaff route (Orange): the ridgeline has a history of many accidents and near misses.

start.name: Bay City Tunnel (just below the turn-off to Alta's upper lot)

published.what: Jaws from the Bay City Tunnel

notes.t: Park just before the turn-off to Alta's upper lot; the stone building is the Bay City Tunnel. Climb the subtle ridge between Emma #1 and Emma #2 to the top of Binx's Ridge: that puts you near the top of Jaws, with Oingo Boingo a little east.
Seen from the north, the chutes are Jaws, Fang, then Oingo Boingo. Fang's entrance is small and rarely skied.
Jaws is expert: the entrance is 50° or more and often corniced, so most people enter from the trees on skier's right. About 900 ft, NW.
Oingo Boingo is advanced, about 34°, NW, 600 ft (WBSkiing). Powder Project measures 480 ft with a 38° max and reaches it from Flagstaff along Emma Ridge.
The Reddit post lists these as easier LCC tours. WBSkiing rates Jaws expert and Oingo Boingo advanced, and both drop north into Days Fork on the Big Cottonwood side.

Ridge above Jaws.source: First crest (USGS 3DEP) walking 135° from WBSkiing.com 2601 (Jaws), uphill from the NW aspect WBSkiing lists

start.name: Bay City Tunnel (just below the turn-off to Alta's upper lot)

notes.t: Four gullies above the Bay City Tunnel, Emma #1 to #4, are well-known avalanche paths. The ridge above them, between Big and Little Cottonwood, is Emma Ridge.

The more common up-track starts on a road about 100 ft east of the tunnel building and climbs the small ridge between Emma #3 and #4. Less than an hour to the ridge. Binx's Ridge itself is the ridge between Emma #2 and #3: intermediate, about 32°, south-facing.
Named for Binx Sandahl, hired as an Alta snow ranger in 1964.

warn.t: SGID maps Emma 1 to 4 as avalanche paths that reach the road.

Emma Ridge above Binx's Ridge.source: First crest (USGS 3DEP) walking 0° from WBSkiing.com 3162 (Binx's Ridge), uphill from the S aspect WBSkiing lists

start.name: Roadside, north side, about 0.3 mi past Snowbird Entry 4

notes.t: An east-facing couloir on Mount Superior, usually skied in spring when avalanche hazard is low, with an early start to top out as the snow softens. When the snow is hard, crampons and an ice axe help.
Park on the north side of the road about 0.3 mi past Snowbird Entry 4, then boot to the base and up the chute: 1,500 ft up, 800 ft of skiing.
The original name is Shane's Chute, after Alta patroller Jim Shane.
This line is OpenStreetMap's "Suicide Chute Ascent" bootpack (way 1382646254), not a computed track.

published.what: Michigan City, to the top of the Honeycomb Cliffs

notes.t: Michigan City is the north side of Grizzly Gulch between Davenport Hill and Black Bess. Runs go from the low 20s to the low 30s in degrees.
Either follow the Twin Lakes Pass track and climb the ridge to the top of the Honeycomb Cliffs, or skin up one of the subridges from the Michigan City flats.
Grizzly Cup, Matilda Bowl and Michigan Gully are named shots on this slope. Quicksilver drops the other way, into Big Cottonwood.
Mind the parking-hours signs at the end of the road.

warn.t: UAC's Grizzly Gulch to Twin Lakes Pass route (Yellow) warns of avalanche terrain above the trail through Michigan City and terrain traps in lower Grizzly Gulch.

properties.name: Birthday Chutes (White Pine)
properties.uac: White Pine to White Pine Lake

notes.t: The Reddit post's "longer tour with fun lines": up White Pine to the Birthday Chutes.

From the lot, cross the footbridge and climb the old road; a switchbacking skin track on the left before the creek is steeper but more direct. On the way out, bear high and skier's right and stay out of the bottom of the drainage.
UAC reports place slides in the chutes at 10,300 to 10,600 ft on NW to NE aspects.

warn.t: UAC rates the White Pine to White Pine Lake skin track Orange, and names the Birthday Chutes as one of the paths it passes under.

April 3, 2026 accident: a skier who had planned on west-facing terrain exited via the Birthday Chutes in poor visibility, triggered a 12–16" wind slab, and was carried about 200 vertical ft and injured. Their lesson: they abandoned a plan built on better evidence than what they used to change it.

properties.name: Pink Pine Ridge
properties.uac: White Pine to Red Pine Lake

notes.t: Cross the footbridge, climb the old road (under 30 min) to where it turns hard left at White Pine creek, take the smaller trail right toward Red Pine for under 10 minutes, then the skin track on the left that zigzags up Pink Pine Ridge. Most of the climb is safe; one short stretch is 34°.

The Pink Pine run is the east side of the ridge: intermediate, about 32°, 700 ft. The entrance is a clearing about 30 minutes up the ridge; drop sooner for tighter aspens or later for open pines. It gets skied out fast.
The Pink Pine Chutes, on the west (Red Pine) side below Rainbow Peak, are much steeper and much less skied.

Pink Pine Ridge.source: WBSkiing.com 3529 (Pink Pine Ridge, below Rainbow Peak)

properties.name: Cardiff Fork: High Ivory & George's Bowl

published.what: Cardiff Pass from the Cardiff Fork trailhead (for scale)

notes.t: Skin the snow-covered Cardiff Fork road past the last cabin (0.5 mi) and the Donut Falls summer lot (0.7 mi), then the jeep road up the west side of the fork. The road is exposed to numerous avalanche paths.
Lower-fork runs like George's Bowl and Catcher's Mitt are the reason to come from Big Cottonwood; upper Cardiff is far easier from Alta over Cardiff Pass.
George's Bowl was originally called Ivory Flakes; today High Ivory and Mid Ivory are often called that.
Coming out, bear skier's left back onto the jeep road low down: with a thin snowpack the creek can be hard to cross.
Some of Cardiff Fork is private land. If confronted, stay calm and polite.

warn.t: UAC's Donut Falls route (Yellow) covers the start of this road: the falls and the last half of that route are exposed to slides from above.

Cardiff Fork Trailhead.source: WBSkiing.com 2647 (Cardiff Fork / Mill D South trailhead, 7,300 ft)

published.what: Gobblers Knob from Butler Fork via Baker Pass

notes.t: The trail crosses the creek right away; the first 10 minutes run under a steep (40°+) west-facing slope. About 20 minutes in, take the left (west) fork toward Circle Awl and the West Butler Saddle, cross into Mill A Gulch, traverse its looker's-right side to Baker Pass, then go east up the ridge.
The Mill A Gulch traverse is exposed to significant avalanche terrain, including White Snake itself.
White Snake and Butler Basin are the Big Cottonwood-side runs. The Mill Creek side skis better but needs more climbing.
The Reddit post calls this a relatively long day, 3 to 4.5 hours.

warn.t: At least four people have died within half a mile of the summit, on the north, east, west and south sides.

March 8, 2025: a party climbing from Baker Pass to the top of White Snake found very reactive wind slabs from 10,000 ft on the leeward ridge, triggered several small slides, and saw natural slides off Mount Raymond.

reddit: the white snake off gobblers knob (3-4.5 hrs)

start.name: Maple Grove winter gate, Mill Creek Canyon

published.what: Alexander Basin from its trailhead (after 3 mi of road)

notes.t: In winter you ski to this trailhead: park at the Maple Grove winter gate and skin 3 miles up the snow-covered Mill Creek road. The road usually closes to cars on November 1.
Most runs in Alexander Basin are easier from Porter Fork.
The Reddit post lists it with Big Cottonwood; it is in Mill Creek Canyon, on the north side of Gobblers Knob.

warn.t: Upper Mill Creek road construction: from March 15, 2026 the road above the Terraces was closed to all public access, walking and biking included. Trails Utah says the upper canyon reopens for winter activities in November 2026; check before you go.

Maple Grove winter gate.source: WBSkiing.com 1001 (Maple Grove trailhead / Mill Creek winter gate, 6,100 ft)

notes.t: A big day: the east summit is 11,330 ft and the trailhead sits at the S-curves in Big Cottonwood.

notes.t: Below the lake is lower-angle terrain. Above it, Mill B South Fork is rocky and full of avalanche hazard, and rarely visited.
Not in your photos by name; it's a UAC-rated route under the onX Monte Cristo and Sundial labels.

warn.t: UAC rates this Orange: the trail runs under avalanche terrain off the Broads/Mill B ridgeline.

start.name: Willow Heights trailhead, 0.4 mi past Silver Fork Lodge

notes.t: UAC rates this Green: 1 mi and 700 ft to the flats and beaver ponds. Avoid the gully on the way up.
A 155-acre conservation area bought in 2001 for watershed and recreation.

start.name: Across from the "Bear Trap Fork Road" sign

notes.t: A good pick when you're short on time or the avalanche danger is up: aspens facing NW to SW, about 28°, 800 ft of skiing. It would be beginner terrain if not for the trees.
A terrain-trap gully low in Beartrap has steep walls that often slide. Take the skin track that climbs right and bypasses it.
Stay out of the area just above the aspens, below the steep rocky hill: it slides often and buried a skier on Jan 24, 2010.

warn.t: UAC rates Beartrap Yellow, for the gully between 8,200 and 8,400 ft and its terrain traps.

Beartrap Aspens top.source: First crest (USGS 3DEP) walking 90° from WBSkiing.com 2163 (Beartrap Aspens), uphill from the W aspect WBSkiing lists

notes.t: Up the private Old Stage Road on the north side of the highway; after the sharp right turn, take the Jeep-road skin track on your left, up a shallow drainage and aspens to "Texas". About an hour to the ridge ("Canada"), under two hours car-to-car.

South-facing and exposed to SW wind and sun, so the snow is often sub-par and the top often scoured; after a storm it can be excellent. Trees are tight near the bottom; the up-track is often the best way out.

warn.t: UAC rates USA Bowl Green if you avoid the terrain "east of the Mississippi", which is steeper and slides often.

USA Bowl top.source: First crest (USGS 3DEP) walking 0° from WBSkiing.com 2206 (USA Bowl), uphill from the S aspect WBSkiing describes

notes.t: Cross the highway to the skin track, join the old jeep road, and just before a thick pine grove take the track right up the East Willow ridge to Willow Knob, then on to the Park City ridgeline above the South Monitor.
Pass Willow Knob on its south side: it is usually scoured, and the north side is more likely wind-loaded.

The South and West Monitors are NE-facing bowls in Summit County: big, long and close to 40°, with cold snow. The West Monitor is a bit steeper, longer and more slide-prone. Snowmobiles are allowed there.
The Reddit post calls these a shorter option. WBSkiing rates both advanced and says the pitch, elevation and NE aspect (cornices, wind loading) make them quite avalanche-prone.

South Monitor top.source: First crest (USGS 3DEP) walking 225° from WBSkiing.com 5228 (South Monitor), uphill from the NE aspect WBSkiing lists

notes.t: WBSkiing calls 10420 a good early-season choice because it's high, and with little snow suggests going up via Brighton Hill or Guardsman Pass and coming back down the snow-covered Guardsman road.

Right after the Guardsman gate, bear right onto the track up the ridge: about 10 minutes to Brighton Hill, about half an hour to the flatter stretch at Picnic Tree. Most runs start from a false summit 500 ft north of the top; the real top has a rock arch.

warn.t: Lane's Leap, the steep clearing below Picnic Tree, and nearby Brad's Run are named for people killed in avalanches (1994 and 1986).
UAC rates the Guardsman road route Yellow: rare slides above the last stretch of road before the pass, and a cornice line.

published.what: Scott's Backdoor from the Guardsman trailhead, to the peak

notes.t: Follow the access road toward Scotts Pass; after about 45 minutes, low-angle glades open on your right for about a third of a mile. Lower slopes are mid-to-upper teens; the upper slopes are 24–32°.
The road back down is flat enough to need poling.
Closed to snowmobiles, but the ridgeline is shared with Summit County where they are allowed, and tracks are common.

Powder Project's line runs from the summit down through Greens Basin to the Spruces: 1.6 mi, 1,499 ft, max 36°, mostly moderate with a few steeper pitches. Expect to skate (or unstrap a splitboard) in Greens Basin.
On the Days Fork trail, a few hundred feet past the meadow below Days Draw, there is a terrain-trap gully that slides often; a skin track usually bypasses it to the right (west).

Inside Alta Ski Area. While uphill travel is open before the season, Alta says backcountry conditions exist and there is no ski patrol, and it can close uphill travel for operations or avalanche mitigation.
During the ski season the only uphill route Alta approves is the Summer Road, which starts at the gate where SR-210 ends and may be used to reach terrain outside the ski area.
OpenStreetMap maps the Baldy Chutes as an Alta run area.

warn.t: Oct 15, 2026: skier-triggered slide on the lower Baldy shoulder, north aspect, 10,200 ft, 18" deep. The first reported slide of this season.
